subject.title: [Feature]: Add realtime video frame transport for provider and gateway relay sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a provider/Gateway realtime video-frame transport now, and if so what consent, validation, payload, logging, and provider-retention boundary should the public SDK/RPC contract enforce?
rationale: Automation can confirm the requested seam is missing, but choosing whether camera frames may transit Gateway/provider/plugin boundaries is a product and security policy decision that will become a public protocol and plugin contract.

options.title: Approve Narrow One-Shot Transport
options.body: Define an additive one-frame contract with explicit consent assumptions, MIME and size validation, no ambient capture, no payload logging, provider-specific mapping rules, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Defer Behind Browser-Direct Proof
options.body: Wait for the browser-direct `describe_view` work at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89127 to land or be rejected before promoting a broader Gateway relay transport.

options.title: Keep Frames Out Of Gateway
options.body: Reject a Gateway relay image transport for now and keep visual context limited to browser-direct or plugin-owned implementations that do not require new core protocol surface.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow One-Shot Transport
recommendation.body: Define an additive one-frame contract with explicit consent assumptions, MIME and size validation, no ambient capture, no payload logging, provider-specific mapping rules, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current assignee and have the strongest recent history across Talk runtime, provider seams, Gateway protocol, and security-sensitive defaults.
